title: An integral surjective cover of an affine scheme on whose closed subschemes constant cohomology vanishes (Stacks 09ZD (1))
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Then there exists a morphism of schemes $\pi:X'\to X$ which is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that for every closed subscheme $Z'\subseteq X'$ (a closed immersion $Z'\to X'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]), every finite abelian group $M$, with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $Z'_{\Et}$, and every integer $q\ge1$, the etale cohomology group [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] $H^q(Z'_{\Et},\underline M)$ is zero. (Stacks' construction: write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=\mathbf Z[x_i]_{i}/J$, let $R$ be the integral closure of $\mathbf Z[x_i]$ in an algebraic closure of its fraction field and $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(R/JR)$.)

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: Let A = Γ(X,⊤), P = Z[x_a] indexed by a in A, K = FractionRing P, L = AlgebraicClosure K, and R = integralClosure P L. Evaluation sends X_a to a, so it is surjective (MvPolynomial.eval₂_X). The affine isomorphism X.isoSpec followed by Spec of this evaluation gives a closed immersion j : X → Spec P (IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective).

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: The map P → L is injective, being the composite P → K → L. Algebraicity over K gives algebraicity over P via IsFractionRing.comap_isAlgebraic_iff. integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_algebraic makes L a fraction field of R; isIntegrallyClosed_iff_isIntegrallyClosedIn gives normality of R. Transfer algebraic closedness along IsLocalization.algEquiv R⁰ L (FractionRing R), so FractionRing R is separably closed.

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: The integral extension P → R induces an integral map f : Spec R → Spec P by IsIntegralHom.SpecMap_iff. Its injectivity follows by applying R → L and the injectivity of P → L. Lying over (RingHom.IsIntegral.comap_surjective) makes f surjective.

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: Take X′ = pullback j f and π = pullback.fst j f. Surjectivity is preserved by base change. Integrality is preserved by base change (Mathlib IsIntegralHom pullback.fst instance); equivalently use integral = affine + universally closed, affine base-change permanence, and the definition of universally closed. The other projection k = pullback.snd j f is a closed immersion by base change of j. This pullback is the same Spec(R/JR) construction as in 09ZD, with J the kernel of evaluation.

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: For any closed immersion i : Z′ → X′, the composite i ≫ k is a closed immersion into Spec R. Apply gabber_absolutely_algebraically_closed to R, its separably closed fraction field, Z′ and i ≫ k. This proves the asserted vanishing for every finite abelian M and q ≥ 1, with no transport of cohomology needed because Z′ itself is unchanged.

split_report.summary: Split along the first paragraph of Stacks 09ZD's proof: (1) presentation A=Z[x_a]/J and construction of R (integral closure of Z[x_a] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field) and X'=Spec(R/JR); (2) integrality of A->R/JR written out directly (reduce the monic equation mod JR) plus Spec of an integral ring map is integral (new leaf, IsIntegralHom.SpecMap_iff); (3) surjectivity directly by lying over (existing pqf-lem-lying-over, Stacks 00GQ) instead of a base change argument, since primes of P/J are primes of P containing J; (4) R normal domain with algebraically (so separably) closed fraction field (new leaf from Mathlib's integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_algebraic and IsIntegrallyClosedIn instance); (5) a closed subscheme of X' is one of Spec R (spec-quotient closed immersion and new leaf for composition, 01QS), then Stacks 09ZC (new unsplit node). The brief's description of 09ZC was inexact: 09ZC is stated directly for any normal integral affine scheme with separably closed function field (no limit over finite sets of variables, no Noetherian hypothesis); 0GY0 is Gabber's H^1 criterion for rings with strictly henselian local rings, not a limit lemma. The statement is kept.
